result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend nearly the same approach: a command palette, hints next to existing actions, prompts after repeated mouse use, a small role-based starter set, rebinding, and measuring adoption. A ties its reasons more closely to this audience (billable time, existing habits) but runs longer and essay-like. B is tighter, explains how to pick the starter set (role plus watching heavy users), and gives a pitch the user can take straight to the PM. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend nearly the same plan: a command palette, contextual nudges, a small role-based starter set, rebinding, and measuring adoption. B covers more of the rubric. It puts shortcut hints next to existing menus and tooltips, ties its argument to billable time, and gives the user a concrete fallback for the PM (a short, skippable intro that is A/B tested). A is more compact, but it is less explicit about showing shortcuts next to the menu items and buttons people already use.
